entries.title: At Hearth, the morning stirs with the ordinary trouble of a market gate blocked by a cart.
entries.text: At Hearth, the morning stirs with the ordinary trouble of a market gate blocked by a cart. Wren turns to Ash, gesturing toward the gate, and says, "Let's go see that cart—maybe we can lift it together." Ash nods, considering the matter, and replies, "Aye, let's see it. A wheel off a cart is a small fix if the axle's sound." Wren tries to communicate the plan to Ash—that they should go see the cart blocking the market gate together. Ash, in turn, signals back a willingness to help with the cart at the market gate.

entries.title: Ash and Wren make their way to the Market, while Old Bramble lingers by his cart, waiting.
entries.text: Ash and Wren make their way to the Market, while Old Bramble lingers by his cart, waiting. Wren turns to Ash with a note of urgency. "Ash, let's head to the gate now—Bramble's just waiting, but the cart's still there." Old Bramble notices the newcomer and speaks up warmly. "Ah, a fresh face! Come to lend an old cart driver a hand, have you? Wheel's snapped clean off — if you've got a clever idea, I'd trade a trinket or two for it."

entries.title: At the Market, old Bramble's cart still sits with its wheel stuck fast, and Bramble waits by it, hoping for a hand.
entries.text: At the Market, old Bramble's cart still sits with its wheel stuck fast, and Bramble waits by it, hoping for a hand. Old Bramble calls to Ash, "Heading to the Hearth, are you? My cart's still stuck here — if you come back with a strong arm or a block of wood, I'll make it worth your while." Ash replies to Bramble, "Let's have a look at that wheel, Bramble. If the axle's sound, we'll have it rolling again before noon." Wren turns to Ash, saying, "Ash — the cart's still here and Bramble's waiting. Where are you headed? We said we'd help with this." Ash answers Wren, "Aye, let's take a proper look. If the axle's bent, we'll need more than muscle—but a snapped spoke can be fixed with a bit of patience and the right wood." Wren then gestures toward the cart, trying to get Ash to look at it together so they can figure out how to help Bramble fix the wheel. Even as the conversation continues, Ash begins moving toward the Hearth, leaving the cart behind.

entries.text: The day at the Market carries the smell of fresh sawdust and iron. Ash makes his way to the bustling square, arriving where the others have gathered. Wren watches the scene unfold, taking in the comings and goings of the Market crowd. Wren, noticing Ash's return, calls out: "Ash, back so soon? Come on, let's get to that wheel before Bramble wears a groove in the ground waiting. I'll hold the cart steady if you work the wood." Old Bramble attempts to get Wren's attention about the Wheelwright's card, offering that he could fetch the wheelwright for a quick fix. The offer hangs in the air as a practical solution for their broken wheel. Wren turns to Ash with a hopeful note: "Ash, look—Bramble's found a wheelwright's card. Want to fetch him? It'd be quicker than lifting the cart ourselves." Ash responds to Wren's suggestion with a plan: "Wren, I'm back at the hearth—need a moment to gather a block of wood. Then I'll head straight to the cart." Old Bramble greets the returned Ash with a sturdy confidence: "Back already, Ash? Good. Let's see what we can do with this wheel — a strong arm and a bit of wood might be all we need."

entries.title: At the market, the three travelers huddle around their broken cart as the evening crowd thins.
entries.text: At the market, the three travelers huddle around their broken cart as the evening crowd thins. Wren tries to get Ash's attention, suggesting they fetch the wheelwright now that they have his card. Old Bramble likewise tries to reach Ash, urging that they fetch the wheelwright from the card for a quick fix. Ash also turns to Old Bramble, suggesting they use the wheelwright's card and fetch him to fix the cart fast. "Aye, fetch the wheelwright — that's the quicker path. I'll stay with Bramble and keep the cart from blocking the gate till you're back." "Aye, fetch the wheelwright — that card says he's a quick fix, and I'd rather trade a trinket than sit here all night. Good thinking, Wren." "That's the plan I hoped for — fetch the wheelwright, save our backs. Let's go together and bring him back to Bramble." "Fair enough, Bramble. If the card's from someone near the forge, fetching him beats my bad back and a chunk of wood. I'll go—Wren, keep an eye on the cart."

entries.title: At the Market, Wren turns to Ash with a plan forming.
entries.text: At the Market, Wren turns to Ash with a plan forming. "Aye, that's the way! Off with you both—I'll keep an eye on the cart and my trinkets till you're back with the wheelwright." "Aye, let's go together—the forge is quicker with two pairs of eyes. Bramble, hold the cart steady till we're back." With Bramble's blessing, Ash sets off toward the Hearth. Old Bramble stays behind, keeping watch over the cart and trinkets.

entries.title: The Market hums around the small group as they gather.
entries.text: The Market hums around the small group as they gather. Wren makes her way over to Hearth, stepping through the crowd. Ash holds their ground, waiting for the others to fall into place. Old Bramble lingers nearby, steady and unhurried. "Good, you're here. Let's head to the forge together."

entries.title: At the bustling Market, the scene unfolds amid the calls of vendors and the shuffle of passersby.
entries.text: At the bustling Market, the scene unfolds amid the calls of vendors and the shuffle of passersby. Old Bramble stands still, patiently waiting. Among the Market's noise and movement, Old Bramble remains rooted in place, holding his ground.

entries.title: At the Hearth, the quiet of the morning settles between them.
entries.text: At the Hearth, the quiet of the morning settles between them. Ash looks to Wren, signalling that it's time to go to the forge for the wheelwright. Wren, catching the intent, signals back that they should head to the forge together now. "Aye, let's go. The forge won't find itself."

entries.title: The Market sprawls around them, stalls and carts crowded with the morning's trade.
entries.text: The Market sprawls around them, stalls and carts crowded with the morning's trade. Old Bramble waits nearby, patient as stone. Wren steps toward Ash, trying to catch their attention—lead the way to the forge, the words hang unspoken between them. "Ash—the forge is that way. Where are you off to? We were to fetch the wheelwright together." But Ash is already moving, heading into the Market's heart.
